title: Notes on the Kings Mountain belt in Laurens County, South Carolina
citation: Overstreet, W.C., and Bell, Henry, III, 1960, Notes on the Kings Mountain belt in Laurens County, South Carolina: South Carolina Division of Geology Geologic Notes v. 4, no. 4 [p. 27-30], map scale 1:181,029.
notes: The paper occupies PDF pages 3-7 (printed p. 27-30 and Figure 1). Pages 1-2 are the volume cover and contents; pages 8-11 belong to other papers in the same issue (Santee Limestone calcium carbonate; Hilton Head Island heavy minerals) and were not recorded. The text layer of pages 3-6 is clipped at the right margin and drops the first paragraphs of pages 3 and 4, so most values were read from the page overview images (image values). Figure 1 (page 7) is a sketch map; legend-only symbols (garnet, kyanite, sillimanite, manganese, diabase dike) were not recorded.

name.note: The authors call it 'probable Battleground schist' in Laurens County

age.quote: SCHIST OF PRECAMBRIAN (?) OR PALEOZOIC (?) AGE OF THE

lithology.value: fine-grained sericite phyllite, muscovite-quartz schist, biotite-muscovite schist, garnet-muscovite schist and some hornblende schist
lithology.quote: THE BELT OF ROCKS CONSISTS OF FINE-GRAINED SERICITE PHYLLITE, MUSCOVITE-QUARTZ SCHIST, BIOTITE-MUSCOVITE SCHIST, GARNET-MUSCOVITE SCHIST AND SOME HORNBLENDE SCHIST.

contacts.value: foliation of the schist is conformable with that of fine-grained feldspathic gneiss, gneissic granite, and hornblende schist to the southeast and northwest of the belt
contacts.quote: THE FOLIATION OF THE SCHIST IS CONFORMABLE WITH THAT OF FINE-GRAINED FELDSPATHIC GNEISS, GNEISSIC GRANITE, AND HORNBLENDE SCHIST TO THE SOUTHEAST AND NORTHWEST OF THE BELT.

depositional_environment.value: originally pelitic sediments with sparse interbedded thin layers of mafic volcanic rocks and very thin discontinuous lenses of carbonate rock
depositional_environment.quote: THIS BELT OF ROCKS APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN ORIGINALLY PELITIC SEDIMENTS WITH SPARSE INTERBEDDED THIN LAYERS OF MAFIC VOLCANIC ROCKS AND VERY THIN DISCONTINUOUS LENSES OF CARBONATE ROCK.

description.value: At the Enoree River the grade corresponds to the biotite-chlorite subfacies of the greenschist facies; it increases to the sillimanite-almandine subfacies of the amphibolite facies between Laurens and the Saluda River
description.quote: AT THE ENOREE RIVER THE GRADE OF METAMORPHISM OF THE BELT OF SCHIST IN LAURENS COUNTY CORRESPONDS TO THE BIOTITE-CHLORITE SUBFACIES OF THE GREENSCHIST FACIES

rank.note: rank reasoned from the lower-case informal name in Laurens County

lithology.quote: THE MANGANESE SCHIST IN LAURENS COUNTY CONSISTS OF MEDIUM-TO COARSE-GRAINED GARNETIFEROUS MUSCOVITE-QUARTZ SCHIST

thickness.value: layers from 1 to 2 inches to 2 1/2 feet thick
thickness.quote: IN LAYERS FROM 1 TO 2 INCHES TO 2 1/2 FEET THICK

depositional_environment.value: manganese deposited with the original sediments
depositional_environment.quote: SUGGEST TO US THAT THE MANGANESE WAS DEPOSITED WITH THE ORIGINAL SEDIMENTS

name.quote: A MASS OF GRANITE NEAR THE CENTER OF THE

description.value: a mass of granite near the center of the belt
description.quote: A MASS OF GRANITE NEAR THE CENTER OF THE

location.value: on S. C. 46 west of Clinton
location.quote: ARE EXPOSED ON S. C. 46 WEST OF CLINTON

description.value: calc-silicate layers, as many as five in one small road cut but none more than 2 inches thick
description.quote: CALC-SILICATE LAYERS, AS MANY AS FIVE IN ONE SMALL ROAD CUT BUT NONE MORE THAN 2 INCHES THICK

location.value: along S. C. 46 just north of the intersection of S. C. 265
location.quote: ALONG THE SAME ROAD JUST NORTH OF THE INTERSECTION OF S. C. 265

description.value: a mass of vermiculite and pegmatite exposed in an opening in hornblende schist
description.quote: A MASS OF VERMICULITE AND PEGMATITE IS EXPOSED IN AN OPENING IN HORNBLENDE SCHIST

location.value: in the cut along the Charleston and Western Carolina Railroad west of S. C. 42, on the southern outskirts of Laurens
location.quote: IN THE CUT ALONG THE CHARLESTON AND WESTERN CAROLINA RAILROAD WEST OF S. C. 42, ON THE SOUTHERN OUTSKIRTS OF LAURENS

description.value: 2 to 3 inch thick layers of muscovite schist and biotite schist with the coarsest kyanite found; individual blades as large as 1/16"x1/4"x3/8"
description.quote: OCCURS IN 2 TO 3 INCH THICK LAYERS OF MUSCOVITE SCHIST AND BIOTITE SCHIST

location.value: on S. C. 6 just south of the Reedy River
location.quote: LAYERS OF HORNBLENDE SCHIST IN AND WEST OF SILLIMANITE SCHIST ON S. C. 6 JUST SOUTH OF THE REEDY RIVER

description.value: layers of hornblende schist containing spindle-shaped masses of sericite, muscovite, and pinnite (?) pseudomorphic after corundum crystals
description.quote: CONTAIN SPINDLE-SHAPED MASSES OF SERICITE, MUSCOVITE, AND PINNITE (?) PSEUDOMORPHIC AFTER CORUNDUM CRYSTALS

strike_dip.value: trends northeastward and dips 15° to 40° toward the southeast
strike_dip.quote: THE FOLIATION TRENDS NORTHEASTWARD AND DIPS 15° TO 40° TOWARD THE SOUTHEAST

description.value: linear features such as elongate clusters of muscovite or sericite on the foliation planes and the axes of small folds
description.quote: LINEAR FEATURES SUCH AS ELONGATE CLUSTERS OF MUSCOVITE OR SERICITE ON THE FOLIATION PLANES AND THE AXES OF SMALL FOLDS

strike_dip.value: strike toward the southwest or south-southwest and plunge about 30° in that direction
strike_dip.quote: STRIKE TOWARD THE SOUTHWEST OR SOUTH-SOUTHWEST AND PLUNGE ABOUT 30° IN THAT DIRECTION

location.quote: BETWEEN CLINTON AND LAURENS THE BELT OF SCHIST AND ADJACENT ROCKS TRENDS MORE EASTERLY

strike_dip.value: N. 60° E. to N. 80° E. with southward dips that rarely exceed 35°
strike_dip.quote: THE FOLIATION STRIKES N. 60° E. TO N. 80° E. WITH SOUTHWARD DIPS THAT RARELY EXCEED 35°

name.note: name cut by the clipped text layer; full text read on the page image

description.value: Several diabase dikes cut across the schist; Figure 1 shows three of these dikes
description.quote: SEVERAL DIABASE DIKES CUT ACROSS THE SCHIST. FIGURE 1 SHOWS THREE OF THESE DIKES

name.quote: AS IF THE SCHIST IS FOLDED INTO A SOUTHWESTWARD-PLUNGING ANTICLINE

certainty.value: interbedded rather than folded relations may produce the distribution observed
certainty.quote: HOWEVER, INTERBEDDED RATHER THAN FOLDED RELATIONS MAY PRODUCE THE DISTRIBUTION OBSERVED FOR THE MANGANESE SCHIST

description.value: the lines of manganese-rich schist appear to be merging toward the southwest and opening toward the northeast
description.quote: THE LINES OF SCHIST APPEAR TO BE MERGING TOWARD THE SOUTHWEST AND OPENING TOWARD THE NORTHEAST
